findings.title: `anchor` carries three unrelated technical senses, none flagged as overloaded at its first (or second) use
locations: src/CLI/Config.jl:8-12 — module docstring: "the two readers of the config's path vocabulary (globs and `file#heading` anchors)"
src/CLI/Init.jl:94 — `derive_config`: "the history and references anchors found by heading"
src/CLI/Seed.jl:47-51 — `select`: "A class's `anchor` here is a third sense of the word ... nor a hat's full-strength flag, which is what `Preflight.resolve_hats` returns."

src/CLI/Preflight.jl:260-262 — `resolve_hats`: "`anchor` is whether the hat runs at full strength rather than on the economy model ... It is unrelated to the `file#heading` anchors of [`Config.resolve_anchor`](@ref)."
src/CLI/Doctor.jl:260-261 — plain `#` comment (invisible to `?name`): "Two unrelated senses of `anchor` meet in this one check."
findings.description: A cold reader who does `?Config` (the sixth file the module includes, long before Preflight or Seed) meets `anchor` defined only as a `file#heading` Markdown-heading locator (`resolve_anchor`), with nothing to suggest the word means anything else. That reading is reinforced at `?Init.derive_config`, which uses the same sense (`references anchors found by heading`). Only much later — at `Seed.select`, itself two files before the file that actually defines it — does a docstring admit the word has a second, unrelated sense (a hat's full-strength flag) and even call itself "a third sense of the word": three genuinely distinct technical meanings of one English word (a Markdown-heading pointer; a boolean meaning "runs at full strength, not on the economy model"; a seed class's placement regex) share the identifier `anchor` across the source, and the source itself (in a `#` comment the REPL never surfaces) concedes "Two unrelated senses of `anchor` meet in this one check." No module docstring — not even `GBGCodingTools`'s own map, which does define `consumer`, `instrument`, `round`, `lane`, `hat`, `Workflow` and `gate` — ever names `anchor` as an overloaded term of art, so nothing in the map warns the reader before the first (Config) sense is met. RULE.DOC.TERMS_DEFINED requires a term of art be defined (or disambiguated) at its first use under a cold read; here the FIRST use is not merely undefined, it is silently one of three incompatible things the same word will later mean.
findings.resolution_hint: Add `anchor` to the GBGCodingTools module map's bound-terms list with a one-line note that the CLI, config and seed subsystems each reuse the word for an unrelated concept (or rename one of the three uses, e.g. `heading_ref`/`hat_strength`/`seed_marker`), and have `Config.resolve_anchor`'s own docstring carry the disambiguating sentence Preflight and Seed already carry, since it is the sense a cold reader meets first.

findings.title: "the quick doctor set" is used as settled terminology 16 files before `QUICK` is defined
locations: src/DocLints.jl:17 — `makedocs`: "Before Documenter runs it runs, in-process, the quick doctor set, the hard scans over the source surfaces..."
src/TestHarness.jl:591 — `gate`: "It runs the quick doctor set and [`GBGCodingTools.gate`](@ref), the generic closure gate..."
src/CLI/Doctor.jl:5-9 — `Doctor` module docstring (first definition): "the `QUICK` set is the subset that holds on a runner with no shim and a detached HEAD."
findings.description: `makedocs` is the third file the package includes (`DocLints.jl`), and its docstring is one of the first things `?makedocs` or a doc-page reader meets. It refers to "the quick doctor set" as though the phrase already names something specific — which it does: the closed selection value `:QUICK` that `Doctor.select`/`Doctor.run`/`Doctor.doctor` accept. But `Doctor`'s module docstring, the only place that says what `QUICK` actually is ("the subset that holds on a runner with no shim and a detached HEAD"), is not reached until file 19 of the 32-file include order — 16 files, and one prior use in `TestHarness.gate` (file 9), after the term is first used as if already common ground. A cold reader has no way, at either earlier site, to tell "quick" is a specific named check-selection value rather than an informal adjective for "the checks that run fast."
findings.resolution_hint: Either move the `QUICK` definition into (or `@ref`-link it from) `GBGCodingTools`'s own module map alongside `gate`/`round`/`instrument`, or have `makedocs`'s and `TestHarness.gate`'s docstrings write `` `Doctor`'s `QUICK` set `` with a link on first mention instead of the bare English phrase "the quick doctor set".

findings.title: `Recall`'s module docstring uses `substrate`, `siteonly` and `roster` a file before `Preflight` defines them
locations: src/CLI/Recall.jl:4-9 — `Recall` module docstring: "...names the hats that were handed two or more seeds and reported none (only a `siteonly` hat is handed a narrowed manuscript; every other substrate gets the whole seeded one)."
src/CLI/Preflight.jl:252-259 — `resolve_hats` (the actual definition): "`substrate` names the view of the corpus the hat works in ... two values ... `full` and `siteonly` (the public pages')."
src/CLI/Preflight.jl:361-363 — `resolve_roster`: "The numbered roster of an instrument: hats for check-consistency, lanes otherwise..."
findings.description: `Recall.jl` (include position 23) is read before `Preflight.jl` (position 24). Its module docstring — the very first thing `?Recall` shows — leans on `substrate` and the specific value `siteonly` as though both are already known package vocabulary, and its `suspect_hats` docstring does the same with `roster` ("the round's roster", with no gloss). None of the three has appeared in any docstring read so far in file order; each is properly defined only one file later, in `Preflight.resolve_hats` and `Preflight.resolve_roster`. A cold reader hits three unglossed nouns in one module docstring that the very next file happens to explain.
findings.resolution_hint: Either reorder the two `include`s (Preflight before Recall), or have `Recall`'s module docstring `@ref`-link `substrate`/`siteonly` to `Preflight.resolve_hats` and `roster` to `Preflight.resolve_roster` on first mention.

findings.title: "surface" is used from its very first appearance as a package concept but never itself defined
locations: src/CLI/Config.jl:8-12 — `Config` module docstring: "the two readers of the config's path vocabulary (globs and `file#heading` anchors)"

src/CLI/Config.jl:139-146 — `surface_files(cfg, key)`: "The files of one surface key of `cfg["surfaces"]` — `rationale`, `pages`, `src`, `ext`, `literate`, `data`, or the compound keys `docs` ... and `all` ..."
src/GBGCodingTools.jl:19 — the only near-gloss, and only as an aside inside the definition of `lane`: "A **lane** is one agent's share of a round — one surface, one territory, or one kind of change."
findings.description: "Surface" reads as ordinary English (a superficial layer) but is a load-bearing package concept: a named, config-declared category of files (`rationale`, `pages`, `src`, `ext`, `literate`, `data`, plus the compound `docs`/`all`) that every scan, the reflection engines, the doctor and the instruments treat as the unit of "what gets read". It is used this way from its first appearance (`Config`'s module docstring, include position 6) onward, but no docstring ever states in one place what a surface conceptually is — a cold reader must reconstruct the concept purely from the enumeration of keys in `surface_files`. The only place the word gets even a parenthetical gloss is a subordinate clause inside the definition of an unrelated term (`lane`) in the main module map, itself read before `Config`'s own docstring supplies the key list.
findings.resolution_hint: Add one sentence to `Config`'s module docstring (or to `GBGCodingTools`'s own map) stating plainly what a surface is — a named category of files the config declares, read as a unit by the scans and instruments — before the key list is presented.
